messages:
Chris - Nova Integrations: Hey team — after last night's model flip our ingest started failing intermittently. ~15% of orders now fail schema validation. Example we just got: 

Chris - Nova Integrations: ```json
{
  "order_id": 118209,
  "line_items": "[{\"sku\":\"A1\",\"qty\":2}]",
  "total": 49.98
}
```

Chris - Nova Integrations: Our parser expects line_items as an array of objects, not a string. Failing with JSONDecodeError and then our validator complains: `line_items: expected array, got string`. This started after traffic was moved to the new model.

Priya (CS): thanks Chris — sorry for the break. Can you confirm the exact endpoint, model id, and any request flags you used? Also roughly when first seen? :eyes: 

Chris - Nova Integrations: Using POST /v1/generate, model=redwood-serve-v2.1, prompt template=order-to-json-v3 (we call it with "force_full_json": true in client). First failures at 2026-03-12T03:22:11Z. Happening for 28/190 requests in last hour.

deploy-bot: deployment redwood-serve-v2.1 promoted to 100% at 2173456600 (canary: 10% -> 100%). Logs: canary completed successfully.

Marta (ML Eng): @Priya @Jamal thanks for the heads-up. Can you paste 2-3 more raw outputs (no client-side reformatting)? Also do you have examples where line_items is present but truncated (e.g., "[...]"), or completely missing? :thinking: 

Chris - Nova Integrations: pasted two more in thread — one with empty string "line_items": "", another with full array but wrapped in string. No truncation seen.

Jamal (SE): Repro steps I ran locally with the same model and prompt: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-serve-v2.1","input":"<ORDER_PAYLOAD>","params": {"force_full_json": true}}'
```
Response I got: 
```json
{"order_id":118210,"line_items":"[{\"sku\":\"B2\",\"qty\":1}]","total":19.99}
```
Same symptom. Looks like a postprocessing step is serializing arrays to strings for some prompts.

Priya (CS): @Marta any known recent change to postprocessors or prompt templates that could cause stringifying nested arrays? We didn't see this during canary smoke so maybe it's input-dependent. :warning: 

Marta (ML Eng): quick check: we rolled a small change to the content steward that toggles a 'compactify' posterior for v2.1 to reduce token count. It runs after model decoding and tries to collapse whitespace/structure. It SHOULD not stringify arrays, but the new rule has a bug when the top-level schema flag `force_full_json` is true — it applies JSON.stringify to any nested value when it detects repeated punctuation. Reproduced locally, failing 3/10 runs for orders with more than 1 item.

Marta (ML Eng): root cause hypothesis: compactify postprocessor uses a regex that treats `[{` as something to escape -> ends up calling JSON.stringify on the array. Fix in progress.

Jamal (SE): Filed PR with fix to postprocessor (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1246). Adding a unit test for nested arrays + force_full_json.

Priya (CS): immediate mitigation: rolling back postprocessor toggle on the production traffic for v2.1. @deploy-bot can you cut traffic back to previous variant?

deploy-bot: routing update requested by Priya. Rolling back compactify toggle for redwood-serve-v2.1 now — traffic will be routed to redwood-serve-v2.0-compatible variant starting at 2173456840.

Marta (ML Eng): hotfix patch ready, will coordinate a monitored re-release once tests pass.

Priya (CS): Chris — I'm going to route your traffic to the compatible variant and monitor. Can you confirm when you see failures stop? I'll keep you posted. :+1:

Chris - Nova Integrations: thanks — seeing failures drop to 0/80 in the first 10 minutes after rollback. Appreciate the quick response.

Priya (CS): follow-ups: 1) postmortem + timeline, 2) improve canary tests to include nested-array samples, 3) add schema-level e2e smoke for customers using force_full_json. I'll open tickets and assign owners.

Marta (ML Eng): adding note — we'll also add a fuzz test for postprocessor to catch any accidental JSON.stringify on substructures.

Jamal (SE): I'll attach the failing request ids and logs to the incident ticket so CS can share with the customer's SRE.

Chris - Nova Integrations: thanks all, will keep monitoring and ping if anything else pops up.
